Uzbekistan Oil & Gas Producers Face Cash Crunch Amid Sudden Price Collapse

Uzbekistan’s oil and gas producers are reeling from a sharp and unexpected collapse in global hydrocarbon prices, leading to significant strains on liquidity across the sector. The ongoing crisis, which began in late May, has left several major producers, including Uzbekneftegaz JSC, facing severe cash flow challenges and mounting concerns over their ability to service existing debts.

The crisis was triggered by a combination of oversupply in regional markets and a dramatic drop in demand from traditional export destinations, resulting in benchmark prices for Uzbek crude and natural gas plummeting by over 35% in just three weeks. As a result, revenues across the industry have fallen sharply, with operators now struggling to cover operational expenses and debt repayments.

“Our current priority is to maintain payroll and essential operations,” said an Uzbekneftegaz JSC spokesperson on Tuesday. “The market conditions are unprecedented, and we are actively engaging with lenders and stakeholders to find solutions.”

Several industry sources report that banks have tightened lending terms in response to the downturn, effectively freezing access to new credit for all but the most secure borrowers. This credit freeze is compounding the crisis for smaller and mid-sized producers, such as Samarkand Oilfields LLC, who are now warning of possible production cuts and project delays.

“Many companies are at risk of breaching debt covenants,” said Khurshid Karimov, an analyst at the Central Asia Energy Report. “With prices at these levels, even the most efficient operators are feeling the squeeze. Refinancing options have dried up, and some firms may be forced into restructuring if the situation continues.”

The Association of Uzbek Oil & Gas Producers issued a statement urging urgent government intervention, calling for tax relief and emergency credit facilities to stabilize the industry. “Without immediate support, we risk a wave of defaults and job losses,” the statement read.

Production activity has already slowed, with several fields in the Bukhara and Fergana regions reportedly operating at reduced capacity. Insiders say capital expenditure programs have been put on hold, and equipment suppliers are experiencing delayed payments.

The government has yet to announce a comprehensive response, though industry executives indicate high-level discussions are ongoing. As the price collapse continues, Uzbekneftegaz JSC and its peers are bracing for continued volatility and mounting financial pressure in the weeks ahead.
